title: Craig Manufacturing Plant Fire 2005
description: On the evening of May 7, 2005, around 8 p.m., John Craig, owner of Craig Manufacturing, arrived at the 59-year-old plant he and his father had built—only to watch it become engulfed in flames. Quick thinking allowed for the safe recovery of the file server, which contained essential engineering drawings, as well as accounting, administration, and human resources files. Immediate action was taken to get the business running again and support the 85 to 90 staff members. The presence of argon, oxygen, and propane gases, combined with flammable materials used in painting attachments, heightened emergency workers’ fears that an explosion could devastate much of Hartland. Consequently, about 400 people were evacuated. Craig Manufacturing produces snow plows, trailers, land-clearing equipment, specialized buckets, and log-handling machinery.
